text:
maria: heads-up — QA found a weird error in the console when streaming function-call responses over SSE. frontend throws a JSON parse error mid-stream.

alex: do you have the raw network payload?

maria: paste from network tab:
```
data: {
  \"role\": \"assistant\",
  \"content\": \"{\\\"choices\\\":[{\\\"delta\\\":{\\\"name\\\":\\\"get_user\\\",\\\"arguments\\\":\\\"{\\\\\\\"id\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"123\\\\\\\"}\\\"}}]}\"\n}


data: {
  \"role\": \"assistant\",
  \"content\": \"}\\n]\"\n}
```

maria: so the JSON object is split across two SSE events; the console tries to parse the first one and fails. QA also saw duplicate prefix after a reconnect resume — looks like resume replays the tail chunk which leads to garbage like `...}]}]}` and token meter counts double.

raj: ugh — this smells like two issues: 1) chunking isn't guaranteeing object boundaries for function-call payloads, and 2) resume path isn't de-duplicating overlap. routing fallback might replay last N bytes.

alex: i pulled logs from the streaming gateway. we currently stream raw bytes as they come from the model backend and flush on kernel output. no explicit framing at SSE layer.

sophia: framing would help — either ensure each SSE event is a complete top-level JSON object or send a newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) safe boundary. also console can switch to a streaming-json parser that tolerates partial chunks and only emits when a full object is assembled.

sam: +1 on streaming parser. quick fix idea for now: when function-call mode is enabled, buffer SSE data until you detect matching braces/quotes and full JSON (simple stack-based check) before calling JSON.parse(). That will reduce parse errors.

jorge: for token metering: we bill per-token as they arrive; resume replay currently re-sends the last 4KB window which can overlap. we need idempotent resume semantics: include a resume-cursor that is a logical token count at server side, not byte offset, and ignore/trim overlapping tokens on resume.

maria: QA also noticed that when a stream switches regions (sticky routing failover), chunks come from two different backends and ordering can be slightly off — console concatenates in arrival order causing malformed JSON.

raj: routing policy should preserve ordering for a given connection. failover must buffer and replay pending chunks only after handshake. if we can't guarantee ordering, we must add sequence numbers to SSE events so the client can reassemble.

alex: sequence numbers are cheap. add `event: chunk\nid: <seq>` headers to SSE and include either full-object flag or partial flag. console can then reorder or wait.

sophia: telemetry gap: current chunk-level metrics only record event count and bytes. we should add `stream_chunk_seq`, `resume_cursor`, and `chunk_parse_status` to logs so we can query how often partial JSON occurs vs complete. also add an alert when parse_errors / 5m > 0.1% for prod.

sam: can we avoid changing billing model for now? jorge's resume-cursor approach might be a short-lived toggle: when resume happens, gateway posts an idempotency token to billing service saying \"resumed-from-token:X\" and billing ignores duplicates for 30s. simple and low-risk.

jorge: doable. i'll prototype an idempotency header `X-Resume-Token: <hex>` that the meter will store for short TTL. if we see same token plus overlapping range, skip double-count.

maria: long-term: backend model runtime should support atomic message boundaries when outputting structured tool calls. open to doing NDJSON at runtime level. this will simplify everything.

alex: action items: 1) add sequence/id fields to SSE events (eng-platform) 2) buffer/stack-based parse guard in console (devex) 3) meter idempotency header in billing (eng-sre/finance) 4) telemetry fields + alert (observability) 5) discuss NDJSON change with runtime team.

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed for sse-metadata headers to 10% of traffic (tags: seq-id, resume-token) — 1766201400.

maria: nice. QA will re-run with canary. please also add a debug flag to the console to show raw events for a session so we can inspect ordering during repro.

raj: i'll own the routing/ordering doc. will sketch failure modes and a fallback handshake that preserves ordering.

sam: i'll spike a small streaming-json parser for the console this afternoon and post a gist.

jorge: prototyping resume-token in meter now, will ping when there's an endpoint.

maria: thanks everyone. QA will post repro + network captures here when available. :raised_hands:
